title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended approach for enterprise customer onboarding, escalation handling, integration best practices, known issues and workarounds, and quarterly business review (QBR) / health check cadence. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and relevant product and engineering owners.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single, repeatable, and auditable process for taking an enterprise customer from contract signature to steady-state operations and renewal.
- Scope: Covers onboarding milestones, integration checklist, runbook for escalations, common issues and mitigations, ongoing health checks, and QBR preparation templates. Applies to hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated, and Private deployments.

1) High-level onboarding timeline (recommended cadence)
1. Contract signed -> Welcome packet & kickoff (day 0–3)
2. Discovery & architecture review (day 3–10)
3. Integration & test plan (day 10–30)
4. Performance tuning & load validation (day 30–60)
5. Production cutover & monitoring handoff (day 60–75)
6. 30/60/90-day QBRs and ongoing cadence (quarterly thereafter)

Roles and responsibilities:
- CSM: primary customer relationship, escalation coordinator, drives QBRs and adoption metrics.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration owner, runbook author for customer-specific configs, assists in performance tuning.
- Support Engineer: second-line support for incidents, owns ticket TTR and RCA followup.
- Product/Eng Owner: triage for product defects, feature requests, and release scheduling.
- Customer Technical Contact (CTC): customer-side integration lead and point-of-contact for architecture/access.

Onboarding checklist (detailed)
A. Pre-kickoff (prior to day 0)
- Send welcome email with docs, support SLAs, contacts, and access forms.
- Create internal onboarding workspace: Slack channel, Confluence page, ticket queue.
- Share network requirements: egress/ingress IPs, firewall rules, if Private/VPC: VPN / peering checklist.

B. Kickoff (day 0–3)
- Agenda: objectives, success metrics, milestones, risk items, roles.
- Deliverable: agreed integration plan and timeline saved to Confluence.

C. Discovery & architecture review (day 3–10)
- Collect: expected qps, latency SLOs, token volume, security requirements (KMS/HSM), compliance needs.
- Map: data flows, PII handling, network topology, authentication model (API keys, mTLS, SSO).

D. Integration & test plan (day 10–30)
- Provide SDK examples, sample prompts, and test harness.
- Validate: authentication, basic requests, streaming responses, function/tool calls, embeddings.
- Run: basic end-to-end tests using staging credentials.

E. Performance tuning & scale validation (day 30–60)
- Load tests: synthetic workload to target 1.5x expected peak QPS.
- Observe: p99 latency, error rate, token cost.
- Apply: batching, caching, model variant selection, quantization profile recommendations from Redwood Optimize.

F. Cutover & monitoring handoff (day 60–75)
- Cutover checklist: rollback plan, runbook owner, monitoring dashboards created and shared.
- Conduct: smoke test in production, validate SLA alerts and run emergency drill.

2) Integration guide (engineer-focused)
Essentials:
- API endpoints: https://api.redwood.ai/v1 (hosted) or customer-specific endpoint for Dedicated/Private.
- Auth: API keys for hosted; for Private/Dedicated, support mTLS/SSO/KMS integration—use provided templates.
- SDKs: reference Node/Python/Go snippets on docs site; include sample retry/backoff patterns.
- Streaming: prefer chunked responses for streaming requirements; ensure client supports partial responses and idempotency keys for retries.
- Embeddings: follow batch size recommendations (default 512 tokens per request) and cache stable inputs.

Sample curl snippet:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Hello world"}'

3) Escalation playbook (operational steps)
Priority matrix (severity mapping):
- Sev 1 (P0): production outage or customer-facing regression preventing critical functionality. Response SLA: initial response 15 minutes, critical paging.
- Sev 2 (P1): severe degradation (high latency >3x SLO, consistent 5xx errors). Response SLA: initial response 1 hour.
- Sev 3 (P2): partial impact or non-urgent feature failures. Response SLA: 4 business hours.
- Sev 4 (P3): cosmetic or minor issues. Response SLA: next business day.

Escalation flow (step-by-step):
1. Triage in Support: gather logs, request IDs, timestamps, SDK versions, and customer impact statement.
2. Assign severity and notify CSM + SE. If Sev 1, page on-call SRE and SE immediately.
3. Create incident channel (Slack) and Confluence incident page with timeline.
4. Short-term mitigations: reroute traffic to fallback model/region, enable reduced batch size, apply circuit-breaker.
5. Engineering debug: capture perf profile, heap/KV cache status, kernel selection logs (if applicable).
6. Provide rolling status updates every 30 minutes for Sev 1, hourly for Sev 2.
7. Post-incident: complete RCA within 3 business days, assign remediation tasks, schedule follow-up with customer.

Escalation contact list (primary):
- Support on-call: support@redwood.ai (see schedule in PagerDuty)
- SE escalation: se-oncall@redwood.ai
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.ai

4) Known issues and common workarounds (living section)
- Issue: Intermittent 429 rate limit spikes during burst traffic.
  Workarounds: implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter; request increased rate limit for Dedicated customers; use local batching in the client.
- Issue: Streaming responses truncated for some client SDK versions.
  Workarounds: upgrade SDK to v2.1.0+, validate chunked transfer support in proxy/load balancer, or switch to polling mode.
- Issue: KV cache warm-up causing higher latency for cold starts.
  Workarounds: pre-warm cache with representative prompts during maintenance window; pin a lightweight warmup endpoint.
- Issue: Private deployment DNS resolution failures after network changes.
  Workarounds: verify DNS TTL and propagation, restart the networking agent on the appliance, check firewall rules for control-plane access.

5) Health checks & QBR materials
Quarterly health check template (CSM led)
- Agenda: Summary of usage (tokens, embeddings), uptime & SLOs, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1k tokens, recent incidents and actions, roadmap items and feature requests, open action items.
- Deliverables: PDF slide deck uploaded to customer Confluence, agreed next steps and owners, updated adoption plan.

Suggested operational metrics to surface in QBR:
- Monthly active endpoints / routes
- Avg tokens per request and total monthly tokens
- p50/p95/p99 latency per model & route
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and root-cause distribution
- Cost per 1k tokens (before/after optimizations)
- Adoption KPIs (features used, embeddings usage)

QBR playbook checklist:
1. Prepare deck 7 business days before meeting.
2. Run data pulls and validate with Eng-Platform dashboards.
3. CSM and SE align on talking points and action items.
4. Share pre-read 48 hours before meeting.
5. Conduct QBR and capture notes+owners in Confluence.

6) Postmortem and continuous improvement
- For Sev 1/2 incidents, a written RCA is required within 3 business days and must include: timeline, root cause, contributing factors, impact, detection time, mitigation steps, and action items with owners and deadlines.
- Maintain an action tracker on the customer Confluence page and review at next QBR.

Appendix
- Network & firewall reference table:
| Component | Ports / Protocols | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| API (hosted) | 443 / TLS | Allow outbound to api.redwood.ai |
| Dedicated control plane | 443 / TLS | Customer-specific domain, consult SE |
| Private appliance | 22, 443, custom control ports | SSH only from approved admin IPs; use bastion host |
